issues.issue: This preliminary-statement recital says the Trust Fund 'is hereby conveyed', while the operative conveyance and its documentary conditions are set out in Section 2.01; a court could be asked whether the recital itself effects the transfer.

The statement that every Certificate other than Class P, CE and R carries the 'obligation to pay Class IO Distribution Amounts' has to be squared with Section 4.22 and the Class IO Distribution Amount definition, which route those amounts through the Supplemental Interest Trust.
The definitions apply 'unless the context otherwise requires', an escape hatch that lets a party argue a defined term carries a different meaning in a particular section.

'Accepted Master Servicing Practices' is defined only by reference to 'customary' practices of 'prudent' master servicers, a standard with no fixed content and a recurring subject of dispute in servicing litigation.

'Assignment Agreement' is defined by reference to three named agreements, while the Exhibit list and 'Bring Down Agreements' definition refer to separate 'Assignment, Assumption and Recognition' and 'Assignment and Recognition' agreements, leaving which instrument is meant open.

The definition bundles assignment/bring-down letters with underlying purchase agreements and asserts that the Originators' representations 'were assigned to the Trustee'; which representations travelled to the Trust, and against whom, is left to be construed.

Section 2.02(d) directs the Trustee to enforce Originator repurchase obligations 'under the related Bring Down Agreement', so the scope of this composite definition controls that remedy and must be reconciled with it.

The definition adds Subsequent Recoveries 'pursuant to Section 5.04(b)', but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex; the recovery mechanics are in Sections 6.04 and 6.05, so the cross-reference is wrong.

The definition of the Class A-3 Certificate grants the right to the Percentage Interest of distributions 'provided for the Class A-2 Certificates', a mis-copied class designation that contradicts the class it purports to define.

The definition defers wholly to Section 4.22 and then adds a 'for purposes of clarity' gloss tied to the first two sentences of Section 4.22(c); if the gloss and Section 4.22 diverge, the priority between them is unresolved.

This definition measures the deduction by 'Realized Losses incurred during the prior calendar month', while every parallel Class M and Class B Principal Distribution Amount uses 'the related Prepayment Period', so the same computation is described two different ways.

Clause (x) lists the Class A, M-1, M-2, M-4 and M-5 Principal Distribution Amounts and omits the Class M-3 Principal Distribution Amount, which every parallel definition includes; the omission changes the computed amount.
The Class P Certificate Account is said to be established 'pursuant to Section 6.09 hereof', but the Agreement has no Section 6.09; the Class P Certificate Account is created by Section 6.08.

The definition gives the Securities Administrator two different offices (Columbia, Maryland and Minneapolis, Minnesota) with the Minneapolis office carved out 'for purposes of certificate transfer purposes', a garbled phrase leaving the boundary between the two offices unclear.

The definition points to the face of the Certificate for either the 'Initial Principal Balance' or 'initial notional amount of this Certificate', with mismatched quotation marks and no rule for classes that have neither.

The Distribution Account is said to be created 'pursuant to Section 5.08', but Article V ends at Section 5.04 and the Distribution Account is established by Section 5.02; the cross-reference has no referent.
Clause (iii) makes eligible 'any other account acceptable to the Rating Agencies', an open-ended catch-all sitting against two closely specified categories, so its reach is uncertain.

The definition permits amendment of the rating requirements 'Notwithstanding Section 12.01' and without Certificateholder consent, which has to be squared with the amendment procedure and consent requirements of Section 12.01.

Whether all recoveries 'expected to be finally recoverable' have been received is left to the Servicer's 'reasonable good faith judgment', a standard with no objective benchmark that controls when losses are realized.
The first Fiscal Quarter is defined as 'December 1 to February 29 (or the last day in such month)', a date that does not exist in most years and is patched by an ambiguous parenthetical.
The definition of 'Insurance Policy' is circular and open-ended, sweeping in 'any insurance policy' plus 'any replacement policy or policies for any Insurance Policies' without a boundary.

Master Servicing Compensation is the Master Servicing Fee 'and any amounts earned on permitted investments in the Distribution Account during the Master Servicer Float Period', but the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes those same float earnings, so the two definitions double-count.
The Master Servicing Fee is a per-loan rate calculation to which float earnings on the Distribution Account are appended, mixing two unlike measures and leaving the fee's content unclear.
The same float earnings are added again by the Master Servicing Compensation definition, so the two provisions cannot both be given effect without duplication.
The amount is whatever the Depositor calculates 'in accordance with the EMC's internal risk management process in respect of similar instruments', an undisclosed and undefined external standard.
The definition describes MERS acting as mortgagee rather than defining a loan, so the defined term 'MOM Loan' does not match its definiens as used in Section 2.01.
The Mortgage is defined as an instrument creating a 'first lien', yet the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition expressly contemplates second lien Mortgage Loans and their CLTV.

The definition preserves loans not in fact transferred where there is 'a breach of the representation contained in Section 2.03(b)(v)', but Section 2.03(b) is a single survival sentence containing no clause (v); the cross-reference has no referent.
The enumerated schedule fields are internally garbled — two different items are lettered '(aa)' and several are '[reserved]' — so what the Schedule must contain is uncertain.
Recoverability is fixed by the 'good faith judgment' of the Master Servicer or Servicer with no objective test, and the residual phrase 'or otherwise' leaves the sources of recovery open-ended.

After listing named offices the definition adds 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers', a catch-all whose reach against the enumerated list is uncertain.

The 'Originator' is defined solely as the party 'set forth in the Mortgage Loan Schedule', but the Mortgage Loan Schedule definition's enumerated fields identify only '(ee) the related Seller' and contain no originator field, so the term has no source.

The final proviso excludes 'investments in units of money market funds pursuant to clause (v) above', but clause (v) is guaranteed reinvestment agreements and money market funds are clause (viii), so the carve-out points at the wrong item.
'Prepayment Assumption' is defined only by reference to the Prospectus Supplement, a document that is not part of this Agreement and is not attached as an exhibit.

The deduction is 'the sum of (a) the related Servicing Fee, (b) the Master Servicing Fee Rate and (c) the LPMI Fee', adding a rate to dollar amounts, and the opening clause ('the amount received from and including the 16th day ... if any, by which') is grammatically broken.

The closing words 'or any replacement policy therefor through the related Interest Accrual Period for such Class relating to a Distribution Date' are grammatically detached and refer to a 'Class' that has no role in a mortgage insurance policy.
Clause (e) picks up Substitution Adjustment Amounts 'pursuant to Section 2.03(d)', but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b) and places the Substitution Adjustment Amount in unlettered text.

The Purchase Price is defined only for loans repurchased 'pursuant to Section 2.02' or purchased under Section 4.21, yet Sections 2.03 and 2.05 require deposit of 'the Purchase Price' on repurchases for breach of representation, leaving those repurchases without a defined price.

Clause (iii) adds 'any costs and damages (if any) incurred by the Trust in connection with any violation of such Mortgage Loan of any predatory lending laws' and is joined by the broken connector 'plus and', leaving the measure of recovery uncertain.

The proviso re-uses the numerals '(i)' and '(ii)' inside clause (ii) for the cap components after already using them for the two principal limbs, making the referents of the numbered clauses uncertain.
A 'REMIC Opinion' turns on whether an action has an 'adverse effect' on a REMIC, a term left wholly undefined and capable of covering anything from disqualification to a tax cost.
The definition breaks off mid-sentence ('the REMIC I Regular Interests and REMIC II Regular'), so the collective term is never completed.
Condition (ii) — a Mortgage Rate 'not less than or more than 1% per annum higher than' the Deleted Mortgage Loan's rate — omits the comparator after 'not less than' and cannot be applied as written.

Condition (ix) requires the Replacement Mortgage Loan to 'comply with each representation and warranty set forth in Section 2.03 hereof', but Section 2.03 contains only corporate representations of the Master Servicer and Securities Administrator, not loan-level representations.
The Reserve Fund is said to be created 'pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof', but Section 6.08 is the Class P Certificate Account and the Reserve Fund is established by Section 4.22(b).
The Depositor's initial deposit is said to be made 'pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof', but the Reserve Fund deposit obligation is imposed by Section 4.22(b), not Section 6.08.

After naming specific offices the definition extends to 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers', so whose knowledge is imputed to the Trustee is left open.
'Seller' is defined as 'Any of EMC and the Sponsor', so which entity is the 'related Seller' owing the cure-or-repurchase duty in Sections 2.02 and 2.03 is not fixed by the definition.
The closing sentence excuses 'Nonrecoverable Servicing Advances', a capitalized term that is nowhere defined in the Agreement, which defines only 'Nonrecoverable Advance'.
The Servicing Criteria may be those 'otherwise mutually agreed to' by four parties 'in response to evolving interpretations of Regulation AB', an open-ended alternative with no fixed content.

The estimate is made by 'EMC or its affiliate', while the Maximum Probable Exposure it aggregates is by definition 'calculated by the Depositor'; the two definitions assign the same computation to different parties.

The parenthetical '(including, but not limited to, recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement)' is attached to 'estimated expenses', so whether repurchase recoveries are Subsequent Recoveries turns on a misplaced clause.
The term is said to have the meaning ascribed 'pursuant to Section 2.03(d)', but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b) and defines the Substitution Adjustment Amount in unlettered text.

This definition states that the Supplemental Interest Trust, Swap Agreement, Swap Account and Swap Administration Agreement 'do not constitute parts of the Trust Fund', while the 'Trust or Trust Fund' definition includes at clause (vi) 'the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates'.

Limb (i) sets the trigger at a percentage 'of the Current Specified Enhancement Percentage' rather than of a balance, and the measuring date is garbled ('as of the as of the last day of the related Due Period'), leaving the test hard to apply.

Clause (vi) puts 'the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates' into the Trust Fund, while the Supplemental Interest Trust definition says the Swap Administration Agreement does 'not constitute parts of the Trust Fund'.
The stated allocation is 93% plus 3% plus 1% to each of five named Classes, which totals 101% of the Voting Rights and cannot be applied as written.

This agreement is said to be 'attached hereto as Exhibit R-3', the same exhibit the Saxon Assignment Agreement definition claims, while the exhibit list assigns R-2 to Saxon; two definitions point at one exhibit.
The definition reads 'the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider', omitting both the date and the counterparty, so the instrument is identified only by the exhibit reference.
The conveyance is of 'the assets in the Mortgage Loans', an odd formulation that leaves unclear whether the Sellers conveyed the loans themselves or some lesser interest in them.

The proviso says 'the Seller may deliver the following documents', but each lettered alternative that follows says 'the Depositor may deliver', so who bears the delivery obligation for substitute documents is inconsistent within the same sentence.

The closing sentence makes cure, repurchase or substitution 'the sole remedies respecting such defect', but limits itself to 'a defect in a constituent document', leaving open whether it also bars remedies for breach of representation.
The sole-remedy sentence sits against Section 2.02(d), which directs the Trustee to enforce 'any other obligations' of the Sellers and Originators under the purchase and Bring Down Agreements.

The Trustee's enforcement duty extends beyond repurchase, cure and substitution to 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation' the Sponsor's Accredited backstop, a catch-all of uncertain reach.
This enforcement duty must be reconciled with Section 2.02(c), which declares cure, repurchase or substitution to be the 'sole remedies' available on behalf of Certificateholders.

The duty is triggered by 'discovery' of a breach that 'materially and adversely affects the interests of the Certificateholders' and requires only 'prompt written notice', none of which is defined or given a time limit or consequence.

This notice paragraph sits inside Section 2.03, whose heading and subsection (b) address only the representations of the Master Servicer and Securities Administrator, yet it governs breaches of the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements enforced under Section 2.02(d).

The closing sentence bars any substitution after the second anniversary of the Closing Date 'notwithstanding anything herein or in any other agreement to the contrary', while Section 2.05(a) postpones substitutions until a default occurs or an Opinion of Counsel is delivered, with no time limit.

The deposit date runs from the month 'during which the related Seller or the related Originator became obligated to repurchase or replace' the loan, without saying whether that obligation arises on breach, on discovery, or on demand.

The survival clause ties 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' to 'delivery of the respective Mortgage Loans and Mortgage Files', but Section 2.03's representations are corporate representations of Wells Fargo unconnected to loan delivery.
The sentence omits the connector before 'the Depositor had good title', so whether the Depositor warrants present title or merely recites a past state of affairs 'following the transfer' is unclear.

The trigger reads 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach', omitting the conjunction and leaving whose discovery starts the notice duty uncertain; the survival is also limited to 'the immediately preceding paragraph'.
The bar on repurchase applies to any loan 'that is not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable', a forward-looking standard with no benchmark or decision-maker identified.

The provision opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and can postpone a repurchase or substitution indefinitely, which cannot be squared with Section 2.03's absolute bar on substitutions after the second anniversary of the Closing Date.
The substitution option is conditioned on 'the conditions in Section 2.03 ... with respect to substitutions', but Section 2.03 states no substitution conditions other than the two-year cut-off.

The permitted purposes end with catch-alls — activities 'necessary, suitable or convenient' and 'such other activities as may be required' — and the closing sentence trails off with 'and this Section 2.07', leaving the limit on the Trust's powers uncertain.

The final sentence — no obligation on the Trustee to assume the duties of Wells Fargo or the Master Servicer 'unless the Trustee has not been able to find a successor servicer' — is a double negative that inverts the intended condition.
The bond and policy need only be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees', a market standard with no stated amount or benchmark.
The paragraph provides for a 'request for release' but then imposes the return obligation by reference to 'Such trust receipt', a document that appears nowhere else in the sentence or the Agreement.

The access sentence is grammatically broken — 'to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — so who is entitled to access is not determinable from the text.

Deposits are made 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.04' and withdrawals 'pursuant to Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04', but Section 5.04 is the Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex and governs neither deposits of insurance proceeds nor withdrawals.
The Master Servicer need only use 'its best reasonable efforts' to keep primary mortgage insurance in force, a hybrid standard that mixes two different efforts benchmarks.
Collections are directed 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05', but the Agreement contains no Section 5.05; Article V ends at Section 5.04.
Foreclosure is required only for loans 'as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection of delinquent payments', a standard with no measure and no decision-maker named.

This section gives the Master Servicer the Master Servicing Fee and, separately, 'all income and gain realized from any investment of funds in the Distribution Account ... during the Master Servicer Float Period', while the Master Servicing Fee definition already includes those float earnings.

The proviso allows early reimbursement of 'unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a capitalized term the Agreement never defines; the operative sentence speaks instead of 'Advances' and 'other unreimbursed advances'.

The paragraph deems any non-compliance an Event of Default and declares that 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary', which cannot be squared with the Events of Default and cure provisions of Section 9.01.

The paragraph makes any Section 4.17 non-compliance an automatic Event of Default and says it 'shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary', which collides with the Event of Default regime of Section 9.01 and with the identical superseding paragraphs in Sections 4.16 and 4.18.

Item (IV) requires a 'Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D) below', but the Sarbanes-Oxley Certification is described in Section 4.18(a)(iii)(D); the cross-reference points to the Form 8-K subsection.

The opening sentence is broken — the parenthetical that should define the collective term 'Additional Disclosure' is never closed ('(collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information in the applicable Exchange Act report is subject to receipt from ...')— so the defined term used throughout Section 4.18 has no definition.
The filing date is 'January 30th of the first year in which the Securities Administrator is able to do so under applicable law', a condition whose satisfaction is left to no one's determination.

The bar on reimbursement of the Securities Administrator's Section 4.18 fees from the Trust Fund sits against Section 4.18(a)(i)(B) and (a)(iii)(B), which make the Depositor responsible for such fees, and against the fee and expense provisions of Section 10.05.
The second indemnity runs only to 'the Depositor and each of its officers, directors and affiliates', dropping the Securities Administrator that the first sentence of the same paragraph protects.
Contribution is to be 'in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties', with no method for weighing fault against benefit.

The paragraph first deems any failure to comply with Section 4.18 an Event of Default requiring immediate termination, then provides that no Event of Default occurs where the failure results from another party's failure to deliver information, so the same paragraph both creates and negates the default.

It also declares that it 'shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary', which cannot be reconciled with the Event of Default and termination scheme of Section 9.01.

The provision allows Section 4.18 to be amended 'Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 12.01' and without Certificateholder consent, which has to be squared with the amendment and consent machinery of Section 12.01.

Delivery of reports and notices by e-mail or telephone under this clause must be reconciled with the formal notice requirements of Section 12.05, to which the same Section 4.18 elsewhere refers for contact details.

Obligations are to be 'supplemented and modified as necessary to be consistent with ... convention or consensus among active participants in the asset-backed securities markets', a standard with no ascertainable content.
Clause (d) provides that 'no amendment of this Agreement shall be required' to change the parties' obligations, which cannot be reconciled with the amendment requirements of Section 12.01.

The option is granted to 'Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder', but the last sentence says 'This right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party', naming a party who holds no such right under the provision.

The Swap Account is here treated as subject to investment instructions given to the Securities Administrator, while the 'Swap Account' definition says it is created and maintained by the Swap Administrator under the Swap Administration Agreement.

This subsection establishes the Reserve Fund and its initial deposit, while the 'Reserve Fund' and 'Reserve Fund Deposit' definitions both say the fund is created and funded 'pursuant to Section 6.08 hereof'.
